title: A Look at Rackham Vale - An OSR setting based on the art of Arthur Rackham
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IrGSyH2wlK0

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *Rackham Vale* from Crowbar Creative, a 150-page OSR setting built from the art of Arthur Rackham, the illustrator of fairy tales and children's literature. It is a review copy, and he is giving it away to a patron — not from dislike, but because his hobby room is full and he rarely gets to GM-led RPGs. He would happily see more settings built from a single artist's work.

Half setting, half bestiary. The Vale is Grimm-flavoured fairy-tale country: seelies, brownies, nixies, selkies, alongside centaurs, dryads and basilisks. The mechanic he finds most interesting is secrets — underlined sentences on perhaps 75-80% of the pages, doled out by the GM or discovered in play, with an apple tree that fruits them and the No-Moon Crone as a major actor. Locations like the Golden River, the King's Head tavern and Absinthe Town come with encounter tables and motivations; a faction chart maps who is hostile, trading or in love with whom; adventure hooks hang off named creatures like the Fish King and the feral owls.

The $40 card bestiary is his pick over the $25 book: stats in old-school ascending and descending AC on one side, roleplaying detail and art on the other. Draw one at random and you have a solo session.

----

A setting built entirely from one artist's images. Whose work would you want a game world grown out of?
